A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPA-Plan research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on four long-context QA datasets, component ablations, planning-behavior analyses and an appendix NLI analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds ReAct comparisons, execution-failure and constraint-quality results, token statistics and evaluator-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same pitfall predictor, constraint-aware planner, syntactic corrector and executor. The corresponding appendix prompts are unchanged after renumbering. Added justification for planning before execution does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate QuALITY, ConditionalQA, LongReason and Qasper, including the same LongReason 16k/32k coverage. The added analyses use existing benchmark coverage without introducing new tasks, domains or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ReAct for all three backbones and four datasets alongside the retained GQA, CoT, Plan-and-Solve and PEARL baselines. ReAct was discussed and cited in v1 but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: v2 adds focused protocols: a Claude-judged audit of 300 constraints from 100 LongReason examples, and a 200-example Qwen comparison using Claude, an alternative GPT-4o prompt and BART-large-mnli. ReAct shares PEARL's action space. The existing benchmark splits, decoding settings and correction budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds execution-failure comparisons, constraint grounding/harmfulness analysis and invalid-constraint error categories. Appendices A.4-A.5 add token-efficiency and judge/prompt/evaluator sensitivity analyses. These substantially expand the reliability checks beyond the retained ablations and reasoning-faithfulness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new percentages and token/call averages continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 and Table 2 scores are retained, while ReAct scores and several diagnostic results are added. New findings include 31.89% ungrounded and 21.93% harmful constraints. Table 7 reports PEARL/PPA-Plan Claude accuracy of 54.5/60.5, a GPT-4o tie at 69.0, and BART NLI scores of 44.4/51.0.

T1.justification: The method equations, bounded correction formulation and existing NLI-analysis definitions are unchanged. v2 adds no mathematical derivations, propositions or proofs; its new constraint labels serve empirical annotation protocols.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the method and long-context QA performance claims. The conclusion drops the broader claim of ensuring reliability and accuracy in agent environments requiring complex planning, modestly narrowing its stated reach.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of noisy constraints as useful structural cues, links structural hallucination and overthinking to question-only prediction, and attributes efficiency gains to constraint guidance. It also explains differences between judges and argues that planning before execution suffices for long-context QA. The existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Tables 14-15 add detailed ReAct action-generation and execution prompts, and Appendix A.4 reports token/call costs. Existing PPA-Plan prompts and Appendix A.1 hardware, quantization, decoding and output-length settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Lewis et al. (2020) BART reference for its alternative evaluator. ReAct was already cited in v1, and the Related Work section and central proactive-versus-reactive positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits, a Methods-to-Baselines heading change, an added planning rationale and acknowledgments, and extensions to Section 4.4 and Appendices A.4-A.5. The existing narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains ReAct rows and a shorter caption. Compact diagnostic/sensitivity tables and two ReAct prompt tables are added, with corresponding renumbering and page reflow. All six existing figures retain their content, and the overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical scrutiny by evaluating ReAct, quantifying previously acknowledged constraint failures, and checking whether the PEARL comparison survives changes of judge and metric. Table 7 appropriately reports a tie under one protocol. These additions improve support for the retained claims, although restricted diagnostic samples and underspecified token/call accounting limit the strength of the new robustness and efficiency conclusions.
